001package dayplanner;
002
003
004import java.util.Scanner;
005import java.io.InputStream;
006
007
008/**
009 * <p>
010 * Console input helper backed by a {@link Scanner}.
011 * </p>
012 * <p>
013 * Read methods display prompts and generally retry invalid input. The stream
014 * constructor also supports scripted input, such as a
015 * {@code ByteArrayInputStream} in a small example program, which is actually
016 * used in {@link dayplanner.Tester} for scripted input.
017 * </p>
018 * <p>
019 * The goal of this class is to make user input as easy as possible to deal with
020 * in application classes. So, this class does a lot of the heavy lifting for
021 * you.
022 * </p>
023 */
024public class Input {
025    private final Scanner SCANNER;
026
027
028    /**
029     * Constructs an <code>Input</code> instance that reads from the specified
030     * stream.
031     * 
032     * @param stream Source of input.
033     */
034    public Input(InputStream stream) {
035        SCANNER = new Scanner(stream);
036    }
037
038    /**
039     * Constructs an <code>Input</code> instance that reads from standard input
040     * (<code>System.in</code>).
041     */
042    public Input() {
043        this(System.in);
044    }
045
046
047
048    /**
049     * Reads and returns an integer from user input, prompting repeatedly until
050     * valid.
051     * 
052     * @return The next parseable integer. Invalid lines are rejected and requested
053     *         again.
054     */
055    public int readInt() {
056        int input = 0;
057
058        do {
059            System.out.print("(integer) > ");
060
061            String line = null;
062            if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
063                line = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
064
065            if (line != null && line.matches("[-+]?[0-9]+")) {
066                try {
067                    input = Integer.parseInt(line);
068                    break;
069                } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
070                    System.out.println("\nInteger value out of range. Try again:");
071                }
072            } else {
073                System.out.println("\nInvalid integer. Try again:");
074            }
075        } while (true);
076        
077        System.out.print("\n");
078        return input;
079    }
080
081
082    
083    /**
084     * Reads and returns a trimmed string from user input.
085     * 
086     * @return User input as a <code>String</code>, or <code>null</code> if end of
087     *         input.
088     */
089    public String readString() {
090        System.out.print("(string) > ");
091
092        String input = null;
093        if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
094            input = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
095        
096        System.out.print("\n");
097        return input;
098    }
099
100
101
102    /**
103     * <p>
104     * Reads and returns a boolean from user input, prompting repeatedly until
105     * valid.
106     * </p>
107     * <p>
108     * Accepts responses beginning with {@code Y}/{@code y} or {@code N}/{@code n};
109     * characters after the first non-space character do not affect the answer.
110     * </p>
111     * 
112     * @return User input as a boolean.
113     */
114    public boolean readBool() {
115        char input;
116        boolean ret;
117
118        do {
119            System.out.print("(Y/N) > ");
120            
121            String line = null;
122            if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
123                line = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
124
125            if (line.isEmpty()) {
126                System.out.println("\nInput cannot be empty. Try typing Yes or No.");
127                continue;
128            }
129
130            input = Character.toUpperCase(line.charAt(0));
131
132            if (input == 'Y') {
133                ret = true;
134                break;
135            }
136            else if (input == 'N') {
137                ret = false;
138                break;
139            }
140            else
141                System.out.println("\nInvalid boolean. Try again; try typing Yes or No.");
142        } while (true);
143        
144        System.out.println(" ");
145        return ret;
146    }
147
148
149
150    /**
151     * Parses a string representation of time in YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM format.
152     * 
153     * @param str The string representing a time in YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM format.
154     * @return A valid {@link Time}, or {@code null} for empty or invalid input. For
155     *         example, {@code 2026/09/15 14:30} produces a time value.
156     */
157    public static Time parseTime(String str) {
158        if (str == null || str.trim().isEmpty())
159            return null;
160
161        String[] components = str.trim().split("[/:,\\s]+");
162        if (components.length < 5)
163            return null;
164
165        try {
166            int y = Integer.parseInt(components[0]);
167            int m = Integer.parseInt(components[1]);
168            int d = Integer.parseInt(components[2]);
169            int h = Integer.parseInt(components[3]);
170            int min = Integer.parseInt(components[4]);
171
172            if (Time.isValidTime(y, m, d, h, min))
173                return new Time(y, m, d, h, min);
174        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
175            return null;
176        }
177
178        return null;
179    }
180
181    /**
182     * Reads and returns a valid <code>Time</code> from user input, prompting
183     * repeatedly until valid.
184     * 
185     * @return A valid {@link Time}; malformed values are explained and requested
186     *         again.
187     */
188    public Time readTime() {
189        do {
190            System.out.print("(YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM) > ");
191            String line = null;
192            if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
193                line = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
194
195            if (line.isEmpty()) {
196                System.out.println("\nTime cannot be empty. Please enter format YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM (e.g. 2026/9/10 17:30). Try again:");
197                continue;
198            }
199
200            Time parsed = parseTime(line);
201            if (parsed != null) {
202                System.out.print("\n");
203                return parsed;
204            }
205
206            // Detailed validation error feedback
207            String[] components = line.split("[/:,\\s]+");
208            if (components.length < 5) {
209                System.out.println("\nInvalid format. Expected: YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM (e.g. 2026/9/10 17:30). Try again:");
210                continue;
211            }
212
213            try {
214                int y = Integer.parseInt(components[0]);
215                int m = Integer.parseInt(components[1]);
216                int d = Integer.parseInt(components[2]);
217                int h = Integer.parseInt(components[3]);
218                int min = Integer.parseInt(components[4]);
219
220                String err = Time.getValidationError(y, m, d, h, min);
221                if (err != null) {
222                    System.out.println("\nInvalid time: " + err + " Try again:");
223                } else {
224                    System.out.println("\nInvalid time values. Try again:");
225                }
226            } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
227                System.out.println("\nTime components must be integers. Try again:");
228            }
229        } while (true);
230    }
231
232    /**
233     * Reads and returns a command string from user input.
234     * 
235     * @return The next line with leading and trailing whitespace removed.
236     */
237    public String readCommand() {
238        System.out.print("(command) > ");
239
240        String input = null;
241        if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
242            input = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
243
244        System.out.print("\n");
245        return input;
246    }
247
248    /**
249     * Prompts the user to press Enter and halts until input is received.
250     */
251    public void pressEnterToContinue() {
252        System.out.println("\nPress enter to continue.");
253        SCANNER.nextLine();
254    }
255}
